bitcoin_node_h1: How to run a Bitcoin node
bitcoin_node_description: Running your own Bitcoin node lets you verify transactions yourself, transact privately, and support the network. This guide covers the hardware and software you need, from a free old-laptop setup to plug-and-play hardware.
bitcoin_node_header_subtitle: Verify your own money. A Bitcoin node lets you check the rules yourself, transact privately, and stop trusting third-party servers.
bitcoin_node_s1_c1: A Bitcoin node is a computer that downloads the entire Bitcoin blockchain and independently verifies every transaction against the rules.
bitcoin_node_s1_c2: Anyone can run a node. The hardware can be as simple as an old laptop, or as turn-key as a pre-built device that arrives ready to plug in. Pick the option that fits your budget and how much setup you want to do:
bitcoin_node_question_1: What is a Bitcoin node and why run one?
bitcoin_node_s2_c1: A Bitcoin node is software that downloads every Bitcoin block ever mined and re-checks every transaction against the protocol's consensus rules.
bitcoin_node_s2_c2: When you run a node, you stop trusting anyone else's view of the blockchain. You verify your own balance, your own transactions, and the 21-million supply cap directly from the source.
bitcoin_node_s2_c3: It also gives you privacy: your wallet can query your own node instead of leaking your addresses to a third-party server.
bitcoin_node_s2_c4: And it strengthens the network. Every additional node makes Bitcoin harder to censor or attack.
bitcoin_node_s3_c1: A Bitcoin node is not demanding. The minimum recipe is a computer that can stay on, an internet connection, and roughly 700 GB of free disk space (the blockchain is ~620 GB and growing slowly).
bitcoin_node_s3_c2: Common setups, from cheapest to easiest:
bitcoin_node_s3_c3: An old laptop or desktop you already own — install Bitcoin Core for free. A Raspberry Pi 5 with an external SSD running Bitcoin Core or RaspiBlitz — under $200 all-in. A small mini PC for better performance and storage. Or a pre-built node from a vendor like Umbrel, Start9, or Nodl that ships ready to plug in.
bitcoin_node_s3_c4: If disk space is tight, every Bitcoin node software supports a pruned mode that throws away old block data after verification. A pruned node still validates everything but only needs ~10 GB of disk.
bitcoin_node_question_3: Do I need to keep it online 24/7?
bitcoin_node_s4_c1: No. You can run a node only when you need it, but uptime matters for two reasons.
bitcoin_node_s4_c2: First, syncing. A node that's been offline has to catch up on all the new blocks before you can use it. The longer it's been off, the longer the wait.
bitcoin_node_s4_c3: Second, privacy and network health. A node that's always online keeps your wallet responsive and helps relay blocks and transactions to other nodes around the world.
bitcoin_node_question_4: Can my node also run Lightning?
bitcoin_node_s5_c1: Yes. Most node software (Umbrel, Start9, myNode, Nodl) can run a Lightning node on top of your base-layer Bitcoin node, using your own validated blockchain as its source of truth.
bitcoin_node_s5_c2: Lightning is a separate network for fast, cheap Bitcoin payments. Running your own Lightning node gives you the same self-sovereignty for payments that a Bitcoin node gives you for savings — but it's more work to maintain (channels, liquidity, backups).
